Consider $△PQR$ shown above. The line segment $\overset{―}{RH}$ is the altitude corresponding to $\overset{―}{PQ}.$ If $m∠PQR={122}^{∘},$ calculate $m∠QRH.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the straight angle must have a measure of ${180}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠HQR+m∠PQR & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HQR+{122}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HQR & ={58}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $△QHR$ is a right triangle. Since its interior angles must sum to ${180}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠QRH+m∠HQR+m∠RHQ & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠QRH+{58}^{∘}+{90}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠QRH+{148}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠QRH & ={32}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
